newsitem.title: USA: HFS off after Merrill cites insider sale.
newsitem.headline: HFS off after Merrill cites insider sale.

text.p: Shares of HFS Inc fell 4-1/8 to 55-3/4 in early afternoon trading amid a report that HFS chief executive Henry Silverman sold 150,000 HFS shares and plans to sell more.
Merrill Lynch analyst Peter Oakes said in a brief research report, "it's our understanding" that Silverman had sold shares. Oakes maintained a buy rating.
A spokesman for HFS was not immediately available for comment.
In the report, Oakes said he expected near-term pressure on HFS shares, noting, "It is never comforting to see an insider selling shares, especially for the first time."
However, Oakes also said that he expected "the stock will continue to be a strong performer once the focus reverts back to the company's impressive prospects."
According to the Merrill note, Silverman's plans include selling another 150,000 shares every quarter for estate planning and charitable purposes.
The stock was sixth on the New York Stock Exchange most actives, with about 1.7 million shares traded.
